sources.entry: Routr - Lightweight SIP proxy, location server, and registrar for a reliable and scalable SIP infrastructure. (Source Code) MIT Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Routr is a lightweight SIP proxy, location server, and registrar for building telephony and SIP infrastructure, deployable with Docker or Kubernetes.
summary.what_it_does: Routr provides core SIP server functions: proxy, registrar, and location service. It supports programmable and configurable routing (intra-domain, domain ingress/egress, peer egress), load balancing across media servers such as Asterisk and FreeSWITCH, and multi-tenant/multi-domain setups with domain-level access control lists. Transports listed are TCP, UDP, TLS, WS, and WSS, with in-memory or Redis location storage and JSON, YAML, or Postgres as data sources. It can be managed through a gRPC API, a command-line tool (@routr/ctl), and a Node.js SDK, and it is extensible through custom Processors and Middleware. Additional listed features include RTPEngine middleware, JWT endpoint authentication for web phones, call message recording and replay, and OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs.
use_cases: Running a SIP proxy and registrar for a telephony carrier
Load balancing calls across Asterisk or FreeSWITCH media servers
Multi-tenant SIP hosting with per-domain access control
Deploying a SIP server on Kubernetes with Helm
Building custom SIP call-routing logic with Node.js processors
how_to_run: Create a directory named routr and add the compose.yaml file from the README
helm repo add routr && helm repo update
notable: Programmable routing with configurable ingress, egress, and intra-domain strategies
Multi-tenant and multi-domain support with domain-level ACLs
Helm chart for Kubernetes deployment and a single-container all-in-one Docker image
Extensible through custom Processors and Middleware, with a Node.js SDK
Built-in OpenTelemetry tracing, metrics, and logs plus call recording and replay
caveats: Region-based routing and STIR/SHAKEN support are listed as unchecked, not yet implemented
The README notes VS Code only forwards TCP ports, so SIP over UDP from a host softphone will not reach a Dev Container
Postgres, Redis, and RTPEngine must be started separately for some workflows and are optional for the basic echo test
Web Application is listed as a planned item, not a current feature
